title: DeepSeek V4 models emit DSML tool calls in message.content instead of structured tool_calls

labels.name: priority:medium
labels.description: For bugs, a serious source of annoyance, but not blocking a large number of users.

body:
## Bug

DeepSeek V4 models (such as `deepseek-v4-flash` / `deepseek-v4-pro`) may emit tool-calling markup using DeepSeek Markup Language (DSML, e.g. `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>`, `<｜｜DSML｜｜r=execute_bash>`) directly into `message.content` instead of OpenAI-compatible structured `tool_calls`. This commonly happens when models fall back to their pre-trained DSML syntax or in non-native tool-calling environments.

## Impact

The OpenHands SDK does not parse DSML markup from `message.content` when `tool_calls` is absent. `classify_response` then classifies the response as `LLMResponseType.CONTENT`, and `_handle_content_response` prematurely sets `state.execution_status = ConversationExecutionStatus.FINISHED` before the requested tool call can be executed. The agent therefore stops without actually invoking the requested tool.

## Reproduction

```python
from openhands.sdk import LLM, Agent, Conversation, Tool
from openhands.tools.terminal import TerminalTool

llm = LLM(model="openai/deepseek-v4-flash", base_url="https://api.deepseek.com")
agent = Agent(llm=llm, tools=[Tool(name=TerminalTool.name)])
conv = Conversation(agent=agent, workspace="/tmp/test-workspace")
conv.send_message("Run echo 42 > answer.txt and say done.")
conv.run()
```

The agent finishes without writing `answer.txt` because the DSML tool call in `content` is never executed.

## Fix

Parse and normalize DSML markup from `content` into standard OpenAI `ChatCompletionMessageToolCall` structures before classification, and strip the markup from `content`. A streaming filter is also needed so DSML tokens do not leak to user-visible `on_token` callbacks.

Superseded by PR #4845 (original implementation by @aibot88) and re-opened as PR #7083 with conflicts resolved and the review-bot's requested changes addressed.

This issue was opened to give PR #7083 a `ready-for-dev`-labelled tracking issue per the repo's PR-description validation rules.

## OpenHands AI triage
**The following comments and acceptance criteria were added by the OpenHands AI agent.**

### Triage
Verified against current `main`: with `tool_calls` absent, `classify_response` (`openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/agent/response_dispatch.py`) classifies DSML markup in `message.content` as `LLMResponseType.CONTENT`, and `_handle_content_response` transitions the conversation to `FINISHED` ("agent replied with a message"), so the requested tool never executes. The failure chain in the Impact section is real on `main`.

Bounded scope: for DeepSeek V4 models, normalize DSML tool-call markup found in `message.content` into standard OpenAI-compatible structured tool calls (when `tool_calls` is empty), strip the markup from the content, and filter DSML fragments out of streaming `on_token` callbacks. Per root `AGENTS.md`, LLM-specific behavior must be gated through the existing model-features registry (`openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/llm/utils/model_features.py`) rather than provider branches in `llm.py`; `deepseek-v4*` is already tracked there, so this extends an established surface.

Non-goals:
- No support for inline tool-call markup from providers other than DeepSeek V4.
- No changes to `classify_response` or agent dispatch logic; normalization happens in the LLM layer so classification sees structured tool calls.
- No prompt-side mitigation, tool-definition changes, or new provider integration.
- PR #7083 / PR #4845 review and merge lifecycle is out of scope for this issue; it only tracks the work.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Given a DeepSeek V4 model response whose message has no structured `tool_calls` and DSML tool-call markup in `content`, the SDK extracts OpenAI-compatible structured tool calls from the markup, strips the DSML markup from the resulting content, and the agent executes the requested tool(s) instead of transitioning to `FINISHED` — validated by an automated test that runs the real SDK path (LLM response normalization → `classify_response` → tool-call dispatch) with recorded/fixture DSML completions such as the issue's `echo 42 > answer.txt` scenario.
- [ ] A DeepSeek V4 response that already contains structured `tool_calls` is returned unchanged: no re-parsing and content untouched.
- [ ] For non-DeepSeek-V4 models, content containing DSML-like markup is not parsed or altered, and classification and execution behavior are identical to `main`.
- [ ] Malformed or unrecoverable DSML markup extracts no tool calls (no partial tool execution), preserves the original content, and the response is handled as an ordinary content response without raising.
- [ ] When streaming with a token callback, no DSML markup fragments reach `on_token`, non-DSML text (including ordinary angle brackets) passes through unchanged, and the assembled stream yields the same normalized tool calls as the equivalent non-streaming response (covered for sync and async token-callback paths).
- [ ] The DeepSeek V4 gating is resolved through the existing model-features registry (including explicit overrides/model metadata, consistent with other feature flags) rather than a provider-specific branch in `llm.py`.
- [ ] Tests are added under `tests/sdk/llm/` mirroring the SDK path (per `openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/AGENTS.md`) and pass with `uv run pytest`.
